title: What a newer OMP client would have to close before it can be pinned
method: The candidate binary was run from an isolated HOME against the production RTX 5090 lane with the documented provider fragment. Because the server refuses unknown and server-managed request fields by design, each rejection would otherwise surface one at a time; a local proxy stripped each refused field in turn and recorded it, so one sweep produced the complete delta rather than one round trip per field.

findings.detail: the candidate sends a prompt-cache affinity hint on every Responses request; the server lists it among the server-managed features it refuses rather than silently ignores. This lane's reuse is session-based, so the hint is redundant, not merely unimplemented.

findings.observed: HTTP 400 additional response fields are not supported (include_not_supported)
findings.detail: the candidate asks for encrypted reasoning content the engine does not emit
the candidate requests a synthesised reasoning summary; reasoning.effort, which it also sends, is supported

the documented fragment maps a local alias to the served model id, and the candidate sent the alias as `model` instead. The key still exists in the binary (106 occurrences), so this is a behaviour change to find in the rebase, not a removed feature

findings.observed: no ninfer* symbols in the upstream binary; the pinned build has 11 occurrences of ninferStatefulResponses
findings.detail: the provider compat layer this product relies on is carried by the fork, not upstream, so a re-pin is a rebase of alphastorm/oh-my-pi onto v18.2.2 - never an adoption of the upstream binary

what_worked_once_the_delta_was_closed.stateful_resume: a planted nonce survived a --continue turn in a fresh session directory: CLIENTPIN-7741 returned exactly
what_worked_once_the_delta_was_closed.note: with the four request-shape items handled, the candidate drives this lane's Responses surface, which is the useful half of the answer: the work is in the request shape and the fork's compat layer, not in the engine

disposition: Do not re-pin yet. A re-pin is a rebase of the client fork onto v18.2.2 that carries the ninfer compat layer forward, suppresses or adapts the three refused request fields for ninfer providers, and restores requestModelId mapping - then a cross-platform rebuild, a new component release, and a re-run of every documented route on every lane, because the compatibility authority pins one client for all of them. The alternative - relaxing the server to accept fields it does not implement - would trade a deliberate product property for convenience and is rejected.
